findings.mechanism: sink_push() (src/sink.c:26) stores each decoded acme_frame pointer from the codec's on_frame callback in the 32-slot replay ring. ring_put() overwrites the oldest slot without releasing the evicted item (the ring is documented as never looking inside items). Nothing in session.c/sink.c/main.c ever releases a frame: the callback never frees or releases it, and sink_close() only frees the pointer array. If the vendor library hands frames to on_frame with ownership (or a refcount) that the consumer must release, every decoded frame is leaked in native memory, one per packet, which matches RSS growing with packet count. The ring only bounds the number of pointers, not the memory they point to.
findings.cause: Frame ownership/release is never honoured: evicted frames in ring_put (and the frames still held at session_close) are never released back to the vendor codec; the ring cannot release them because it is item-agnostic.
findings.evidence: Code reading only. I could not build or run ./capture: the vendor library (libacmecodec) and <acme/codec.h> are not on this machine (filesystem search found nothing), so the frame ownership contract could not be checked and no growth was measured. make test builds and passes for the ring alone. Under the opposite contract (frames borrowed and only valid inside the callback) the code has a dangling-pointer bug instead of a leak. Fix to verify: release the evicted item on overwrite and the remaining ones in sink_close.
